subject: Clarifying default logs: what we store, deletion SLA, and opt-out flow
messages:
From: Sarah Lin <sarah.lin@retrosys.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Retrosys Security Team <security@retrosys.com>
Date: Sun, 14 Nov 2027 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Questions on default logs, residency, and deletion path

Hi Jordan —

Thanks for taking this. As part of our procurement security review we need a concise description of Redwood's default logging behaviors for the hosted API. Specific asks from our InfoSec team: 

- Exactly which items are stored by default for a typical text-generation request (request metadata, full prompts, responses/outputs, model name, client IPs, headers)
- Default retention window for each class (requests/metadata, prompts, outputs, embeddings)
- Whether any artifacts are retained outside our selected region (we are US-only)
- Deletion workflow and SLA if we request purge of past data (what gets removed, how long until it’s unrecoverable)
- Opt-out/opt-down options available for hosted customers (headers, API flags, account-level toggles)

I attached a small sample payload to illustrate (retrosys-data-sample.json). If you can respond with a short playbook-level answer we can attach it to our vendor assessment. If it helps, we can hop on a quick call.

Appreciate it,
Sarah
Security Analyst, Retrosys

Attachments: retrosys-data-sample.json (sample request payload)
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Lin <sarah.lin@retrosys.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 14 Nov 2027 10:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Questions on default logs, residency, and deletion path

Hi Sarah —

Thanks for the clear list. Below is a concise, playbook-style summary we use for vendor assessments. I’ll include Marissa and Priyom for details and operational items.

TL;DR (hosted API default)
- Stored by default: request metadata (timestamps, model id, route), billing tokens, partial request headers. Prompts and responses (request/response) are retained by default for 30 days for debugging, quality, and abuse monitoring. Embeddings are stored for 90 days by default.
- Residency: We store data in the customer-chosen region for primary storage (US/EU/APAC). Short-lived telemetry (aggregated metrics, synthetic traces) may be routed to a central metrics cluster for 7 days; no raw prompts/outputs are replicated across regions by default.
- Deletion SLA & workflow: When a purge request is received we run a cascade: primary index deletion -> object store purge -> cache invalidation -> audit index scrub. Typical completion: 30 calendar days for complete irreversible removal; we provide interim confirmation when primary indexes are cleared (usually within 72 hours).
- Opt-out options: Hosted customers can request prompt/output non-retention via an account toggle or by setting an API header (X-Redwood-Retention: ephemeral). For accounts requiring stricter controls we offer Dedicated and Private deployments with configurable retention = 0.

Notes / caveats:
- Billing and minimal telemetry (billing tokens and usage meters) are retained for accounting and fraud detection; we can minimize those to hashed aggregates on request.
- For compliance reasons we may keep a compact audit record (hashes + timestamp) to show proof of deletion; those hashes are non-reversible and do not contain plaintext prompts/outputs.

I’m attaching a one-page playbook for your security team with the above and a proposed opt-out header example. Marissa / Priyom — please flag anything inaccurate or operationally infeasible.

Best,
Jordan
Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood-retention-playbook-v1.pdf
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Lin <sarah.lin@retrosys.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 14 Nov 2027 12:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Questions on default logs, residency, and deletion path

Sarah —

Adding operational detail to Jordan's summary from an enterprise perspective:

- Default windows are configurable under enterprise contracts. The 30 / 90 day defaults are our hosted-product baseline used for free-tier and standard paid accounts; enterprise Dedicated customers commonly set prompts/outputs to 0–7 days.
- For US-only residency: our control plane manages region routing. When you select US region we commit to never store full-text artifacts in non-US storage. We do, however, keep a short-lived global index for routing and throttling (no PII, retention 7 days).
- Deletion flow specifics: after a purge request we create a deletion job with a unique job id and report state changes back to the customer. Complete wipe involves: (1) mark-and-sweep index removal, (2) object-store lifecycle deletion (may be subject to provider GC window ~24–72h), (3) downstream analytic mirrors removed or redacted. We provide a deletion report artifact.

If you need formal language for your contract (SLA paragraph and indemnity notes) let me know and I’ll route to legal.

Marissa
Senior Product Manager, Redwood Inference
From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Lin <sarah.lin@retrosys.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Nov 2027 09:07:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Questions on default logs, residency, and deletion path

Quick technical clarifications from the runtime side:

- Caches & KV: The inference runtime maintains a KV-cache for recently used key-value pairs (attention caches) to speed up streaming generation. These caches are ephemeral in memory and are not written to durable logs by default. If you enable persistent prefix-caching as a customer feature, keys are hashed and stored; full prompt content is not written unless the customer opts into request logging.
- Backups & object-store GC: Our object-store provider may keep deleted objects for a provider-specific window (soft-delete) — our deletion job triggers provider API calls to remove versions and then requests immediate GC; we document expected provider windows in the deletion report.
- Audit trail: to support some compliance audits we keep non-reversible digests (SHA-256) and timestamps for up to 365 days by default unless contractually removed. These digests are returned in the deletion report to prove prior existence without revealing content.

Happy to provide a short runbook for your infra/security team explaining the deletion job lifecycle and sample API calls.

— Priyom
Applied ML / Runtime Team, Redwood Inference
